data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"No autonomous reclamation protocol can guarantee never to silently displace completed evidence, because the absence of a terminal record is observationally equivalent to both incomplete execution and completed-but-lost execution; an external adjudicator must render the verdict.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The external adjudicator may be unavailable, introducing unbounded reclamation delay","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checkpoint chain may omit the precise state transition where evidence was finalized","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The evidence namespace may contain entries that are semantically valid but not causally linked to this workspace","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The protocol durably records deterministic checkpoint hashes of the workspace at regular intervals alongside the problem input specification. All completed evidence is published to an external evidence namespace with strong durability. After crash, the workspace is quarantined rather than reclaimed. An external adjudicator compares the checkpoint chain, the evidence namespace, and the problem input to render a binding verdict on whether evidence was completed. Reclamation is permitted only upon explicit adjudicator signature.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
